 Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF ( QQQM ) was the sole ETF buying on Tuesday, Oct. 27, with no funds selling. QQQM deployed $252.0 million in gross trades, all of it net buying, increasing 101 positions and decreasing none. The fund's assets under management stand at $110.98 billion.

 The largest buy was NVIDIA Corp ( NVDA ), which gained 94,605 shares worth $20.6 million and now makes up 8.18% of the portfolio. Apple Inc ( AAPL ) followed with 57,290 shares added for $19.9 million, then Microsoft Corp ( MSFT ) at 29,155 shares for $15.5 million, Micron Technology Inc ( MU ) at 12,240 shares for $11.4 million and Amazon.com Inc ( AMZN ) at 42,330 shares for $10.7 million. None of the trades opened a new position or exited one, and there were no reported sells. 
 How does QQQM invest? 
 Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF ( QQQM ) is an Equity US fund in the Equity asset class holding 101 stocks, with 46.8% of assets in its 10 largest holdings. Technology accounts for 58.8% of the classified stocks, followed by Communication Services at 11.3% and Consumer Cyclical at 10.8%, and the portfolio is 100.0% large-cap. It charges an expense ratio of 0.15%, and its top holdings are NVIDIA Corp at 8.18%, Apple Inc at 7.89%, Microsoft Corp at 6.15%, Micron Technology Inc at 4.51% and Amazon.com Inc at 4.25%. The fund has a GF Score of 88, a P/E of 28.59, a P/B of 7.7, a dividend yield of 0.42% and a year-to-date return of 18.53%.
